articles.title: Micro-ondas: o que pode explodir, espirrar ou pegar fogo | G1
articles.standfirst: Ovos, líquidos e alguns tipos de embalagem estão entre os itens que exigem atenção na hora de esquentar a comida.
articles.summary: O uso incorreto do micro-ondas com ovos, líquidos e embalagens inadequadas pode causar explosões e incêndios, exigindo atenção redobrada com a segurança no dia a dia.
articles.body:
Mulher colocando copo para aquecer água no micro-ondas — Foto: Freepik

Esquentar comida no micro-ondas não é livre de riscos: ovo explodindo e água fervente espirrando podem acontecer com qualquer pessoa.

E a culpa normalmente não é do aparelho, mas, sim, do uso descuidado. Em casos extremos, a falta de atenção pode acabar em queimaduras e ferimentos graves.

O aquecimento no micro-ondas pode aumentar a pressão dentro dos alimentos. Quando existe uma casca ou película impedindo a saída do vapor, isso pode levar à explosão.

Veja a seguir quais são os principais cuidados para isso não acontecer com você, segundo a nutricionista Elke Stedefeldt, professora do Departamento de Medicina Preventiva da Unifesp e colaboradora da Associação Brasileira de Nutrição.

Alimentos com casca ou pele podem explodir

🥔 Batatas, tomates, salsichas e outros alimentos inteiros podem acumular pressão durante o aquecimento. Por isso, devem ser furados com um garfo ou cortados antes de ir ao aparelho, de acordo com orientações de fabricantes como Consul, LG e Electrolux.

🥚 No caso do ovo, o cuidado é ainda maior: não se deve colocar no micro-ondas um ovo com casca nem um ovo cozido inteiro.

Se o ovo estiver cru, ele deve estar sem casca e com a gema furada. Já o ovo cozido precisa ser cortado antes de ser aquecido.

🛍️ A mesma atenção vale para alimentos vendidos em embalagens fechadas, como alguns pratos congelados. A embalagem deve ser aberta antes de entrar no aparelho , sempre seguindo as instruções indicadas pelo fabricante do produto.

Água pode espirrar mesmo sem parecer que está fervendo

Outro risco é o da chamada ebulição tardia. O líquido pode chegar a uma temperatura muito alta sem apresentar as bolhas que normalmente indicam que está fervendo.

💨 Segundo a explicação de Stedefeldt, isso acontece porque o micro-ondas aquece a água dentro do líquido sem provocar a mesma movimentação observada em outros métodos de aquecimento.

O problema pode aparecer quando a porta é aberta, quando o recipiente é movimentado ou quando alguma substância é adicionada ao líquido. A água pode começar a ferver de maneira repentina e espirrar.

Evite recipientes com gargalos estreitos, como garrafas;

Depois do aquecimento, espere cerca de 30 segundos antes de retirar o recipiente;

Tenha cuidado ao mexer ou adicionar ingredientes ao líquido já aquecido.

Também é importante não exagerar no tempo ou na potência. Quanto mais tempo o alimento fica no aparelho, maior a chance de passar do ponto de aquecimento necessário.

🍞 Pães, amendoim e outros alimentos com pouca umidade também pedem atenção. Se ficar tempo demais no micro-ondas, podem superaquecer e até pegar fogo .

Por isso, vale seguir o tempo indicado para cada alimento e, quando necessário, interromper o funcionamento para verificar o preparo.

Nem todo recipiente pode entrar no aparelho

Além da comida, é preciso prestar atenção ao material usado para aquecê-la.

✅Vidro e cerâmica: estão entre as opções mais seguras, mas mesmo nesses casos é preciso evitar peças frágeis ou com partes metálicas.

⚠️Plástico: só devem ser usados recipientes de plástico identificados como próprios para micro-ondas. Também é preciso conferir as especificações do produto.

⚠️Isopor: por ser um tipo de plástico, não deve ir ao aparelho a menos que o recipiente seja explicitamente indicado para esse uso.

❌Metal: recipientes e utensílios de metal podem produzir faíscas e danificar o aparelho.

❌Papel: embalagens e recipientes de papel também podem pegar fogo e, por isso, não devem ser colocados no aparelho sem que o fabricante indique que são adequados para esse uso, como nas embalagens de pipoca de micro-ondas.

🕵️‍♀️Caso especial: papel alumínio. Exige cuidado, não devendo envolver completamente o alimento nem ficar próximo às paredes do micro-ondas.

Porém, embalagens de alumínio próprias para alimentos podem ter regras específicas de uso no aparelho. A Associação Brasileira de Alumínio recomenda, entre outros cuidados, que a embalagem esteja sem tampa, não encoste nas paredes e fique a pelo menos 5 cm delas.

Para evitar acidentes, queimaduras e danos ao aparelho, a regra mais importante continua sendo simples: antes de colocar qualquer alimento ou recipiente no micro-ondas, confira as orientações do fabricante do aparelho e da embalagem do produto.

Abaixo, veja modelos de micro-ondas por R$ 500 a R$ 660 e acessórios para usar no aparelho desde R$ 15 a R$ 60. Os itens foram consultados em setembro, nas grandes lojas da internet.

articles.title: Contagem da USP aponta público bem menor em blocos de carnaval do que números divulgados em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Diferença ocorre porque pesquisadores contam pessoas simultâneas com método científico, enquanto números oficiais não detalham como são calculados; distorção prejudica o planejamento da cidade.
articles.summary: Diferença ocorre porque pesquisadores contam pessoas simultâneas com método científico, enquanto números oficiais não detalham como são calculados; distorção prejudica o planejamento da cidade.
articles.body:
A cantora Daniela Mercury desfila com o bloco Pipoca da Rainha pela Rua da Consolação, na região central da capital paulista, no encerramento do carnaval 2026 em São Paulo. — Foto: DANIEL TEIXEIRA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

A estimativa de público do bloco Pipoca da Rainha , comandado por Daniela Mercury, foi de cerca de 20 mil pessoas, segundo levantamento feito por pesquisadores da Universidade de São Paulo (USP). O número é cem vezes menor do que os 2 milhões de foliões divulgados pela organização do bloco.

O cálculo foi realizado pela professora Mariana Aldrigui, especialista em políticas de turismo urbano da USP, em parceria com o Monitor do Debate Político, núcleo de pesquisa do Centro Brasileiro de Análise e Planejamento (Cebrap). A metodologia é a mesma usada há anos pelo grupo para estimar público em grandes manifestações políticas no Brasil (leia mais abaixo).

Segundo pesquisadores, a contagem real de público é importante porque orienta o planejamento e a segurança da cidade. Números inflados podem distorcer decisões sobre transporte, policiamento, limpeza urbana e banheiros químicos, além de comprometer a transparência no uso de recursos públicos.

O desfile comemorou os 10 anos do bloco de Daniela Mercury em São Paulo e ocorreu no domingo (22), na Rua da Consolação, no Centro, durante o pós-carnaval. O show começou por volta das 14h e reuniu foliões ao longo de toda a tarde.

De acordo com o relatório técnico, os pesquisadores estimaram a presença de 20 mil pessoas, com margem de erro de aproximadamente 12%, o que representa uma variação de cerca de 2,4 mil pessoas para mais ou para menos.

“Mesmo considerando a margem de erro e possíveis oscilações ao longo do desfile, o público ficou muito distante da casa dos milhões”, afirma Mariana.

O estudo também analisou outro megabloco do carnaval paulistano, o Sertanejinho do Teló, na região do Ibirapuera, e chegou a um número semelhante: 21 mil pessoas, com margem de erro de cerca de 2,5 mil. A organização do bloco, porém, estimou o número de 1 milhão de foliões.

De acordo com a professora, a escolha dos blocos levou em conta critérios operacionais e técnicos, principalmente a disponibilidade de pilotos e drones nos dias dos desfiles e a possibilidade de delimitar com precisão a área ocupada pelos blocos.

Megabloco da cantora Pabllo Vittar levou multidão ao Ibirapuera, na Zona Sul de SP — Foto: Fábio Tito/g1

Segundo a pesquisadora, a dinâmica do bloco da Daniela Mercury contribuiu para uma estimativa mais estável. Por isso, o estudo afirma que nenhum dos blocos analisados ultrapassou 100 mil pessoas no total, mesmo considerando todo o período do desfile.

“Não houve uma substituição total de público ao longo do tempo. As pessoas chegaram e permaneceram. O próprio formato do circuito dificulta entradas e saídas rápidas”, diz.

Procuradas pela reportagem, as equipes do Pipoca da Rainha e do Sertanejinho do Teló não explicaram, até a última atualização, como a contagem foi realizada.

O tema causa discussão há anos, sobretudo em protestos políticos, porque faltam critérios claros e transparência na contagem de público. Segundo Mariana, pesquisadores, como os da USP, usam métodos técnicos e margem de erro, enquanto o poder público e organizadores divulgam estimativas sem detalhar como chegam aos números.

“Ter um número mais próximo da realidade não diminui o carnaval. Pelo contrário, ajuda o poder público a planejar melhor segurança, transporte e serviços urbanos com base em dados concretos”, afirma Mariana.

A contagem foi baseada em fotografias aéreas captadas por drones, posicionados em ângulo perpendicular ao solo (90 graus), o que reduz distorções de perspectiva e permite identificar cada pessoa individualmente.

📷 Drones tiram fotos na posição vertical; a divisão é feita por perímetro, podendo ser de um quarteirão inteiro ou de meio quarteirão.

🖥️ Um software excluí imagens sobrepostas, para não contar as mesmas pessoas duas vezes.

➕ Cria-se uma grande foto na horizontal, juntando todas as fotos verticais.

👥 Um software treinado para contar cabeças aponta uma estimativa do número de pessoas na imagem.

No caso do bloco da Daniela Mercury, as imagens foram feitas em três momentos distintos do desfile, nos seguintes horários:

Segundo o documento das análises, as fotos cobriram toda a área ocupada pelo bloco na Rua da Consolação. Para evitar sobreposição, as imagens foram organizadas em mosaicos, permitindo a visualização completa do espaço.

Antes da captura das imagens, os pesquisadores delimitaram com precisão a área do evento, com base em um estudo técnico da Fundação para o Desenvolvimento Tecnológico da Engenharia (FDTE), contratado pela própria Prefeitura de São Paulo, que mapeia os trechos oficialmente destinados aos blocos de carnaval.

As imagens foram analisadas com o software Point to Point Network (P2PNet), um sistema de inteligência artificial desenvolvido por pesquisadores da Universidade de Zhejiang, na China, em parceria com a empresa Tencent. O programa foi treinado com bancos de dados internacionais e também com imagens de multidões brasileiras anotadas por pesquisadores da USP.

“É um método que permite contagens precisas mesmo em áreas densas e irregulares, como blocos de carnaval”, explica Mariana.

Segundo a pesquisadora, a dinâmica do bloco da Daniela Mercury contribuiu para uma estimativa mais estável. “Não houve uma substituição total de público ao longo do tempo. As pessoas chegaram e permaneceram. O próprio formato do circuito dificulta entradas e saídas rápidas”, diz.

Por isso, o estudo afirma que nenhum dos blocos analisados ultrapassou 100 mil pessoas no total , mesmo considerando todo o período do desfile.

No pré-carnaval, o bloco da Ivete Sangalo levou 1,2 milhão de pessoas ao Ibirapuera , segundo dados divulgados pela PM. A polícia explicou que o cálculo foi feito com base nas imagens aéreas captadas pelo helicóptero e pelos drones da PM, associadas ao georreferenciamento da área do Parque Ibirapuera e à análise técnica da densidade de público por metro quadrado.

Mariana afirma, no entanto, que não há transparência sobre como são feitas as contagens divulgadas por organizadores, pela Polícia Militar ou por órgãos da prefeitura. Segundo ela, não existe um documento público que explique, de forma técnica, como se chega a números como 1 ou 2 milhões de pessoas em um único bloco.

Ela também critica o uso do termo “foliões”, que pode inflar os dados ao contabilizar a mesma pessoa várias vezes ao longo do dia. “Uma pessoa pode ir a três blocos diferentes e ser contada três vezes. Isso só não é um problema se a metodologia for explicitada, o que não acontece”, afirma.

“Quando se fala em milhões de pessoas simultaneamente, isso impacta decisões sobre segurança, transporte, banheiros, limpeza urbana e o funcionamento da cidade. Sem método claro, o número vira peça de marketing.”

Para ilustrar a diferença de escala, a pesquisadora comparou os números divulgados no carnaval com grandes shows recentes. Segundo ela, o show de Bad Bunny realizado em São Paulo no último fim de semana estava “ultralotado”, mas reuniu cerca de 90 mil pessoas, número muito inferior aos milhões citados em alguns blocos.

“A desocupação de um estádio com 90 mil pessoas leva quase duas horas. Isso mostra como o nosso olhar não está treinado para lidar com milhões: volumes de dezenas de milhares já são enormes”, afirma, ao argumentar que estimativas na casa dos milhões não se sustentam do ponto de vista físico e operacional.

articles.title: Quatro dias após pós-Carnaval, banheiros químicos seguem no Ibirapuera | G1
articles.standfirst: Circuito recebeu megablocos como os de Ivete Sangalo, Pedro Sampaio e Pabllo Vittar. A SPTuris informou que os sanitários e demais estruturas montadas para os blocos estão sendo retirados ao longo da semana.
articles.summary: Circuito recebeu megablocos como os de Ivete Sangalo, Pedro Sampaio e Pabllo Vittar. A SPTuris informou que os sanitários e demais estruturas montadas para os blocos estão sendo retirados ao longo da semana.
articles.body:
Quatro dias após o fim do pós-Carnaval, cerca de 20 banheiros químicos instalados para atender os foliões continuam no circuito do Ibirapuera, na Zona Sul de São Paulo . O flagrante foi feito pela TV Globo nesta quinta-feira (26).

Além dos sanitários, a equipe também encontrou acúmulo de lixo na área , que recebeu megablocos como os de Ivete Sangalo, Pedro Sampaio e Pabllo Vittar.

Neste ano, a Prefeitura reduziu a contratação de banheiros químicos de 24 mil para 16 mil diárias.

A diminuição foi percebida pelo público, que relatou longas filas e estruturas sujas ou sem condições de uso durante a folia.

Procurada, a São Paulo Turismo (SPTuris) informou que os banheiros e demais estruturas montadas para os blocos estão sendo retirados ao longo da semana e que o serviço é acompanhado diariamente.

Quatro dias do fim do pós-carnaval, ainda há banheiros químicos instalados no Ibirapuera. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: Como hit 'Carnaval' colou nas redes e marcou a festa no Brasil em 2026 | G1
articles.standfirst: Canção original faz parte do álbum 'Coisas Naturais', de Marina Sena, lançado em março de 2025, mas foi versão estendida, com Psirico, que estourou no país.
articles.summary: Canção original faz parte do álbum 'Coisas Naturais', de Marina Sena, lançado em março de 2025, mas foi versão estendida, com Psirico, que estourou no país.
articles.body:
"Hoje cê pode me esquecer, é carnaval no Brasil." Se você está nas redes sociais ou curtiu a folia em algum canto do país, provavelmente leu esse verso cantando. Ele abre a música "Carnaval", da cantora mineira Marina Sena, que foi reproduzida milhões de vezes durante a festa.

A canção original faz parte do álbum "Coisas Naturais", lançado em março de 2025 , mas foi a versão estendida, turbinada pela percussão de Psirico, que estourou no país.

Só no Spotify, foram 15,5 milhões de reproduções até esta quarta-feira (23). No YouTube, 4,5 milhões . A música ainda foi a trilha sonora de 140,9 mil publicações no TikTok e de 83 mil reels no Instagram.

A versão repaginada com o toque baiano de Psirico é uma das seis faixas do EP "Marinada" , que chegou às plataformas digitais no último dezembro , às vésperas do carnaval.

Na última segunda-feira (23), os três artistas que dividem a composição com Marina Sena – Enzo Dicarlo, Janluska e Pedro Lucas – publicaram um vídeo em que mostram como a música foi produzida (veja abaixo) .

Natural de Taiobeiras, no Norte de Minas, a cantora e compositora Marina Sena já se consolidou como um dos nomes mais importantes da música pop no Brasil .

A mineira ganhou projeção nacional com a edição do álbum "De primeira" , de 2021, com os hits "Me Toca" e "Por Supuesto".

Depois, vieram outros dois álbuns de estúdio: "Vício Inerente" (2023) e "Coisas Naturais" (2025).

Além de dar nome ao EP lançado no fim do ano passado, Marinada é o bloco que a cantora levou às ruas de Belo Horizonte no carnaval deste ano. Cerca de 400 mil foliões acompanharam a atração, que lotou o entorno do Mineirão, na Pampulha , no dia 15 de fevereiro.

"Sempre foi meu sonho estar aqui no carnaval de BH, ter o meu trio aqui. Finalmente aconteceu [...]. Para mim, o carnaval de BH é o melhor do Brasil, eu amo muito, sou fã!", disse Marina Sena à imprensa.

O tamanho do público surpreendeu até mesmo a organização do bloco . Os foliões reclamaram de dificuldade de circulação e acesso a água, além de som baixo.

articles.title: Marron Brasileiro recupera celular furtado durante show com João Gomes | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantor usou rastreador para localizar aparelho, que chegou a ser encontrado em dois bairros do Recife.
articles.summary: Cantor usou rastreador para localizar aparelho, que chegou a ser encontrado em dois bairros do Recife.
articles.body:
O cantor Marron Brasileiro recuperou o celular que foi furtado enquanto ele participava da "drilha" de João Gomes , no último fim de semana, no Centro do Recife . Em publicação nas redes sociais, o artista agradeceu aos fãs pela mobilização para encontrar o aparelho (veja vídeo acima) .

"Aí, ó, apareceu! É só ter paciência, resiliência, saber conversar com as pessoas, ter educação, humildade acima de qualquer coisa, que as coisas acontecem. Apareceu, chegou à minha mão. Quero agradecer a todos que se empenharam", declarou.

O caso aconteceu no domingo (22), durante o desfile da Drilha São João Gomes, que reuniu uma multidão na Rua da Aurora. Em post no Instagram, o cantor explicou que estava se apresentando com o anfitrião da festa, em cima do trio elétrico, quando deu por falta do celular.

Na publicação, ele disse que o aparelho era rastreado e tinha sido localizado no bairro de Água Fria, na Zona Norte do Recife. Depois, o dispositivo foi encontrado em São José, na área central da cidade.

No novo vídeo, postado na quinta-feira (27), Marron não explicou como o aparelho foi recuperado. O g1 entrou em contato com o artista, mas, até a última atualização desta reportagem, não obteve resposta.

"Obrigado, gente, e uma dica: cuide dos seus celulares, coloque a segurança necessária etc. E, caso acontecer, paciência, resiliência, calma, que encontra", afirmou.

Na legenda, ele reforçou o alerta para as medidas de segurança que ajudam a evitar esse tipo de ocorrência.

"Utilizem todos os recursos de segurança disponíveis em seus aparelhos, como rastreamento, bloqueio remoto e registro nas plataformas oficiais. Essas ferramentas são fundamentais e podem fazer toda a diferença", escreveu.

Marron Brasileiro recuperou celular furtado enquanto ele participava da 'drilha' de João Gomes, no Recife — Foto: Montagem/g1

Nascido no bairro da Mustardinha, na Zona Oeste do Recife, Jefferson de Alencar Santos, o Marron Brasileiro, tem 47 anos de carreira e é um dos principais compositores de frevo de Pernambuco.

Entre os seus maiores sucessos, estão composições como "Nas ondas do desejo", "É tanto amor", "Galera do Brasil" e "Arreia a lenha".

O artista cresceu ouvindo Reginaldo Rossi e Fernando Mendes e começou a carreira cantando em bares. Ele também foi um dos homenageados do carnaval do Recife em 2025 .

articles.title: Celulares e até smartwatch: os itens perdidos no carnaval de Olinda | G1
articles.standfirst: Central de achados e serviços do município tem, ao menos, 1.028 objetos que foram resgatados nas ladeiras. Apenas 30% dos produtos catalogados foram entregues.
articles.summary: Central de achados e serviços do município tem, ao menos, 1.028 objetos que foram resgatados nas ladeiras. Apenas 30% dos produtos catalogados foram entregues.
articles.body:
Imagem de arquivo mostra ladeira do Sítio Histórico de Olinda em terça de carnaval — Foto: Leo Caldas/g1

No sobe e desce das ladeiras de Olinda , é comum os foliões perderem objetos pessoais enquanto brincam o carnaval. Segundo a prefeitura, a central de achados e perdidos do município ficou com, ao menos, 1.028 itens guardados após a folia de 2026.

Entre os pertences de moradores e turistas que foram resgatados na Cidade Alta, estão documentos, cartões, bolsas, celulares e até um smartwatch (veja lista abaixo) .

O setor de achados e serviços começou a funcionar em janeiro, durante o período de prévias carnavalescas, e é mantido pela Secretaria Municipal de Segurança Cidadã.

De acordo com o órgão, até o momento, 549 pessoas procuraram o serviço e cerca de 360 objetos foram entregues — o que equivale a aproximadamente 30% do total de itens catalogados.

Para verificar se tem algum objeto guardado lá, o folião pode entrar em contato com a central pelo WhatsApp, no número (81) 98979.0054, ou se dirigir à sede da secretaria, que fica na Avenida Santos Dumont, no imóvel 177 - Lado B, no bairro do Varadouro.

Segundo a Secretaria de Segurança Cidadã, entre os itens encontrados durante o carnaval, estão:

19 cartões do Vale Eletrônico Metropolitano (VEM)

cinco Certificados de Registro e Licenciamento de Veículo (CRLVs);

36 cartões do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS);

articles.title: Luis César Bueno fala sobre plano de mobilidade urbana | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PT defendeu plano estadual voltado às regiões metropolitanas de Goiânia e Brasília, integração de corredores e tarifa zero durante sabatina.
articles.summary: Candidato do PT defendeu plano estadual voltado às regiões metropolitanas de Goiânia e Brasília, integração de corredores e tarifa zero durante sabatina.
articles.body:
Em sabatina realizada pelo jornal O Popular e pela rádio CBN, o candidato Luís César Bueno ( PT ) defendeu a criação de um Plano Estadual de Mobilidade Urbana com foco prioritário nas regiões metropolitanas de Goiânia e de Brasília. Durante a entrevista, o candidato destacou a necessidade de reestruturar o transporte coletivo em Goiás e retomar investimentos em corredores estruturantes.

Segundo o candidato, o planejamento prevê conectar e integrar os corredores metropolitanos de transporte público, além de recuperar a política de implantação de BRTs nas principais rotas intermunicipais. O petista também afirmou que pretende implantar o passe livre (tarifa zero) para os passageiros do sistema.

Além da mobilidade urbana, o candidato respondeu a perguntas sobre propostas para infraestrutura, educação e segurança pública.

Eleições 2026: Luis César Bueno fala sobre plano de mobilidade urbana e retomada da política de implantação dos BRTs — Foto: Reprodução/TV Anhanguera

"Nós pretendemos instituir um plano estadual de mobilidade urbana muito focado na região metropolitana de Goiânia e na região metropolitana de Brasília. Implantar um sistema entre os corredores metropolitanos do transporte coletivo. É importante retomar a política de implantação dos BRTs. Nós pretendemos implantar também a tarifa zero", afirmou Luís.

O candidato também abordou questões econômicas e fiscais da administração estadual, apresentando seu posicionamento sobre a política de arrecadação do estado e os impactos da reforma tributária em Goiás.

articles.title: Chuva preocupa moradores em rua com muro de contenção em Teresópolis | G1
articles.standfirst: Parte de uma antiga estrutura de contenção cedeu após as chuvas do fim de semana. Prefeitura afirma que o novo muro não foi comprometido e que local é monitorado com a Defesa Civil.
articles.summary: Parte de uma antiga estrutura de contenção cedeu após as chuvas do fim de semana. Prefeitura afirma que o novo muro não foi comprometido e que local é monitorado com a Defesa Civil
articles.body:
As chuvas do fim de semana voltaram a preocupar moradores da Rua Jaguaribe, na Fazendinha, em Teresópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, por causa das condições da encosta e de uma antiga estrutura de contenção que fica sob o novo muro construído no local.

A região enfrenta problemas relacionados a deslizamentos desde a tragédia de 2011. Em abril deste ano, parte da rua cedeu novamente. Após o deslizamento, a Prefeitura construiu um novo muro de contenção, entregue em junho, com o objetivo de solucionar o problema. Pouco tempo depois, no entanto, novos transtornos foram registrados.

Na semana passada, um entupimento na rede de água pluvial provocou um novo afundamento no pavimento da rua. Segundo a Prefeitura, o reparo foi realizado no dia seguinte.

Agora, moradores também estão preocupados com uma parte da antiga estrutura de contenção, que cedeu em um dos pontos, e com as condições do barranco ao lado.

Prefeitura diz que novo muro não foi comprometido

O secretário municipal de obras, Davi Serafim, afirmou que a estrutura do novo muro de contenção continua adequada e não foi comprometida pelo deslocamento da parte antiga.

Segundo o secretário, a retirada do trecho do muro antigo que ficou sob a nova estrutura ainda está sendo estudada. A avaliação é que o serviço precisa ser realizado com segurança para evitar novos problemas na encosta.

Sobre as reclamações relacionadas ao entupimento da rede pluvial e às condições do barranco, a Secretaria Municipal de Obras informou que o local segue sendo monitorado em conjunto com a Defesa Civil.

A Águas da Imperatriz também foi procurada e informou que as questões relacionadas à galeria de água pluvial são de responsabilidade do município.

articles.title: Kolkata Metro authorities caution content creators against phone-sticking and running stunt
articles.summary: Kolkata Metro warns creators not to attempt viral “phone-sticking and running” reel stunt, citing platform safety risks; many such videos are edited illusions.
articles.body: KOLKATA: A reel that appears to show a passenger casually leaving his phone stuck to a moving Metro window before running in the direction of the moving train with a popular tune playing in the background is now making its way into Kolkata’s social-media ecosystem, prompting Metro authorities to caution commuters against attempting the stunt.The trend, which recently prompted a warning from Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), has been replicated on the Metro systems in several Indian cities. In Kolkata, too, similar “phone-sticking and running” videos are being noticed on social media, with officials warning that such attempts could put the creator and fellow commuters at risk, besides damaging the phone and causing inconvenience on platforms and inside coaches.“We urge commuters not to treat Metro trains and platforms as a film set. The concern is not only the phone: someone running along a departing train could collide with another commuter, lose balance or create a dangerous situation near the platform edge. We have asked RPF officials and station staff to be cautious about such attempts and are also appealing to passengers to discourage anyone attempting such stunt,” said a Metro spokesperson.The craze exploded nationally after Delhi-based influencer Nikhil Kochar posted a reel on the Delhi Metro’s Yellow Line. Grooving to the tune of ‘Manma Emotion Jaage’ from ‘Dilwale’, the video showed Kochar dancing on the platform before appearing to stick his phone to the train and run after it as it departed. The reel crossed 135 million views in two days and spawned a stream of imitations.But the apparent stunt is largely an illusion. There is no reliable evidence that Kochar’s phone remained attached to the moving train throughout the sequence. Viewers spotted reflections and differences in image quality and concluded that the final footage was shot from inside the coach and edited with the platform sequence. In the format being copied, the creators across the country have started to pose beside the train while a separate camera records from inside, creating the impression that the phone stuck to the window is filming the entire sequence.The trend has since travelled beyond Delhi. Similar “phone-sticking and running” videos have surfaced in Bengaluru.The practice has also been replicated with local trains, buses and even auto-rickshaws.Regular commuters echoed the concern, saying a few seconds of viral footage was not worth creating a risk for others. “These days people shoot reels and videos at public places without the consent of other passengers often creating disturbance for them. What looks like a clever camera trick online can become dangerous when people try to copy it for real and can create a bigger trouble for fellow commuters,” said Puja Sengupta, a regular commuter.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Govt to build hostels for 10,000 students, says Delhi CM Rekha Gupta
articles.summary: Delhi govt plans hostels for 10,000 students after Satya Niketan collapse, offering safe, affordable housing with security, audits, and PPP construction.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Days after the Satya Niketan tragedy, chief minister Rekha Gupta Tuesday announced that Delhi govt would construct hostels for 10,000 students to “provide them a safe, supportive place to stay, so they can study with peace of mind and move closer to the future they came here to build”.“Lakhs of students come to Delhi for study; they get admission but not hostels... (They) will be provided safe and economic accommodation. These hostels will be made for girls as well as boys from any university,” Gupta said, adding that hostels are required for making Delhi a big education hub. The scope of the initiative will be expanded as per the growing need, chief minister’s office said.On Sept 6, a five-storey building being used as a paying guest facility for students collapsed in Satya Niketan near Delhi University’s South Campus, killing seven people, including five DU students. The incident brought back into focus the issue of lack of safe and adequate accommodation facilities for students and triggered demands for institutional housing facilities.The construction is already under way or has been proposed at several institutions, including Ambedkar University, Dhirpur, GB Pant Engineering College and Polytechnic, Indira Gandhi Hospital and Medical College, and Delhi Sports University. Various departments, such as health, higher education, and women and child development, are getting the hostels constructed under the public-private partnership model. Govt will also conduct a survey of colleges that have sufficient space for hostel construction.An official said hostels would have essential facilities, including Wi-Fi, 24-hour electricity and water supply, study rooms, libraries and hygienic messes. Round-the-clock security will be ensured through CCTV surveillance and biometric entry systems. Fire safety measures and regular structural audits will be accorded the highest priority to ensure a safe and secure living environment for students, the official said.“We will make such hostels where parents from different parts of the country can leave their children without worry. The students also need not worry about food and accommodation, rather they can concentrate on their dreams,” said CM.Delhi faces a severe shortage of institutional hostel accommodation. DU, for instance, has around 2.5 lakh regular students, many of whom come from outside the city, but currently has hostel capacity for only 7,210, forcing a large number of students to live in unsafe and uncomfortable PG accommodations at high rents. Many of these buildings have been constructed in densely populated areas in violation of building norms. DU has planned to expand the capacity to 12,754 seats, still falling short of the requirement.Soon after the Satya Niketan incident, a high-level meeting, chaired by lieutenant governor TS Sandhu and attended by CM, was held to examine the issue. Education minister Ashish Sood recently promised a student delegation that govt would introduce comprehensive legislation and regulations for paying guest accommodations within two months. articles.title: FDA suspends Mumbai's iconic Cafe Mondegar licence over hygiene lapses
articles.summary: FDA suspends Mumbai’s 94-year-old Café Mondegar licence over hygiene and structural violations; nine other eateries also face action ahead of festivities.
articles.body: MUMBAI: FDA on Tuesday suspended the licence of Café Mondegar, the iconic 94-year-old restaurant in Colaba, for hygiene and structural violations.Some of the issues flagged included temperature control failures—hot foods kept below 60°C, cold storage above 5°C, improper thawing, and slow cooling—damp floors; defective drainage near food preparation areas, posing cross-contamination risks; and inadequate equipment sanitisation.The restaurant declined to comment, saying its manager had left for the day.FDA also suspended the licences of nine other establishments— Ruhafza Bakery (Khar West), Chandru’s Pure Ghee Sweets (Andheri West), Sharma Dairy & Fast Food (Andheri West), Punjabi Chandu Halwai LLP (Grant Road East), Shri Narayan Dairy (Vile Parle West), Gulshan Dairy Farm (Khar West), Tribhuvan Dairy Farm (Ghatkopar West), Mahavir Cashew & Foods Pvt Ltd (Ghatkopar East), and Agrawal Sweet Mart (Jogeshwari East).Officials said keeping in mind possible large-scale adulteration or hygiene violations during the festive season, a joint FDA-BMC workshop was held for 110 self-help groups engaged in making modaks. They said assistant commissioners and food safety officers guided attendees on good hygiene and manufacturing practices, as well as methods to prevent cross-contamination.Such workshops were also arranged for office-bearers and volunteers of various Ganesh mandals across the city. “This was to ensure that prasad distributed to devotees is prepared and served in a safe, hygienic and healthy manner, taking necessary food safety precautions. articles.title: Jarange’s Mumbai stir: Health concerns grow after 18-day fast; Fadnavis flags protest timing
articles.summary: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange heads to Mumbai on day 18 of hunger strike, plans fast at Azad Maidan; police permission pending as Fadnavis urges no Ganeshotsav disruption.
articles.body: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange on Tuesday began his march from Antarwali Sarati in Jalna district to Mumbai, setting the stage for another showdown with state govt. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis appealed for a protest that does not disrupt Ganeshotsav.Eighteen days into his indefinite hunger strike, Jarange left his Jalna village around noon and announced that he would resume his fast at Mumbai’s Azad Maidan on Sept 19. His convoy is expected to travel more than 400 km through Beed, Ahilyanagar, Pune and Raigad before reaching the state capital.The march comes amid uncertainty over permission for the proposed protest. Mumbai Police have already rejected two applications seeking permission for an indefinite hunger strike at Azad Maidan. A fresh application, this time seeking permission for a gathering of 50 people and assuring compliance with all conditions, remains under consideration.Addressing reporters on Tuesday, Fadnavis said, “Police had rejected Jarange’s application seeking permission to protest in Mumbai. Police will decide on any fresh application based on its merits.”The chief minister maintained that govt had already addressed most of the movement’s demands. “Govt has accepted 12 of the 13 demands raised by the Maratha protesters that were legally valid,” Fadnavis said, adding that legal constraints prevented action on the remaining demands.“I feel that instead of taking such a position during the festive days, they should take a decision so that people do not face any inconvenience,” he added.Jarange, however, accused govt of repeatedly failing the Maratha community and vowed to continue the agitation.“I will not surrender before govt,” he said, adding the protest was aimed at securing justice for Maratha youth and future generations.Earlier in the day, Jarange underwent a health check-up, offered prayers at a Hanuman temple and then set out with a small convoy of supporters. Crowds gathered along the route, raising slogans and greeting the activist. The response slowed his movement considerably, with the convoy covering barely 22 km in nearly six hours before heading towards Patoda in Beed district.Concern over Jarange’s health continues to grow. He has reportedly stopped accepting medical treatment and saline after police denied permission for the Mumbai protest. His supporters fear his condition may worsen during the journey.His wife, Sumitra Jarange, blamed govt for forcing him back onto the streets. “Govt is incapable of understanding us. If they had taken decisions earlier, he would not have set out for Mumbai. When every person has the right to agitate, how can the govt deny permission for our agitation?” she asked.The state has deployed a Special Protection Unit officer and a constable to accompany Jarange throughout the march.Deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde, speaking publicly on the issue for the first time since the Mumbai agitation was announced, said, “Govt is taking care that Ganesh devotees do not face any inconvenience. Earlier, 58 morchas were held, and the world took note of those morchas. No one was ever inconvenienced or allowed to face any inconvenience through those morchas. Therefore, we want everyone to ensure that no one is inconvenienced during Ganeshotsav,” Shinde said.The Jarange agitation was also discussed at Tuesday’s cabinet meeting. Minister Shambhuraj Desai defended the administration’s handling of the issue, saying it had honoured commitments made during talks with the activist and had undertaken extensive work to trace Kunbi records through the Justice Shinde Committee.OBC groups and MoS Ashish Jaiswal too backed govt’s stand on Jarange’s agitation on Tuesday, arguing that most of his demands have already been met and accused him of prolonging a now “non-issue” movement. However, NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar blamed govt for failing to engage meaningfully with the Maratha quota activist.MoS Ashish Jaiswal said govt had established the required scrutiny mechanism for Maratha reservation claims and that grievances should be addressed through legal channels rather than street protests. He alleged that Jarange’s continued agitation was being driven by “malice and prejudice” and was creating unnecessary confusion.OBC Mahasangh president Babanrao Taywade said most of Jarange’s demands had been fulfilled except those pending before courts. He argued that the agitation was unlikely to receive public support and accused Jarange of holding people hostage to a protest.Rohit Pawar, however, said govt was responsible for the impasse. He argued that the lack of sustained dialogue had pushed Jarange back onto the streets and questioned the police decision to deny permission for a protest in Mumbai. “Holding a protest is a constitutional right,” Pawar said.— with inputs from Chaitanya Marpakwar & Abhishek ChoudhariStay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. articles.title: Modi told Xi India, China must be sensitive to each other’s core concerns: Govt
articles.summary: India News: PM Narendra Modi raised Indian concerns in ties with China with President Xi Jinping when the leaders met last week on the sidelines of the BRICS summ.
articles.body: PM Narendra Modi raised Indian concerns in ties with China with President Xi Jinping when the leaders met last week on the sidelines of the BRICS summit, saying both sides need to show sensitivity to each other’s core concerns, according to the Indian government.The assertion by MEA was in response to a question about the Chinese readout that quoted Modi as saying India’s position on Tibet and Taiwan had not changed and India does not allow anyone to carry out anti-China activities on its soil.“Prime Minister referred to Indian concerns as well and underlined that both sides should show sensitivity to each other's core concerns and be guided by the three mutuals, mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity,” said spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. Modi had told Xi that border peace forms an essential basis for taking the relationship forward.Amid repeated cases of border strife with China, India had stopped publicly articulating its One-China policy 16 years ago. However, in practice, India’s position on both Tibet and Taiwan has remained unchanged under successive governments.Government maintains its policy on Taiwan is clear and consistent, as it facilitates and promotes interactions in areas of trade, investment, tourism, culture, education and other such people-to-people exchanges.On Tibet, India continues to recognise that the Tibet Autonomous Region is part of the territory of the People’s Republic of China, as stated in the Declaration on Principles for Relations and Comprehensive Cooperation signed by then PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and Premier Wen Jiabao in 2003. The declaration also stated that India does not allow Tibetans to engage in anti-China political activities in the country.According to the Chinese readout, Modi had also told Xi that India followed an independent foreign policy and its approach to China had nothing to do with any third country. Indian side did not mention Tibet or Taiwan in its readout. Interestingly, India on this occasion dropped China’s ‘friends, not rivals’ formulation that it used in its readout of the Modi-Xi meeting in Tianjin last year.After external affairs minister S Jaishankar’s meeting with his counterpart Wang Yi in Manila in July this year, China had attributed similar remarks to Jaishnakar about India respecting China’s sovereignty. The MEA later clarified that Jaishankar had told Wang it was India which should be raising sovereignty issues with Beijing. He said India does not violate China’s sovereignty in any manner, but China remained in illegal occupation of Indian territory in Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh since 1963, where India’s right is officially acknowledged even by China.“Also, there are Chinese projects on territories in Jammu and Kashmir that belong to India, and we object to that,” said Jaiswal, days after Jaishankar-Wang meeting, alluding to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Intended to kill her’: Chilling details emerge as cops say Gurgaon car collision with biker was deliberate
articles.summary: GURGAON: Kalyan Bainsla (33), who rammed his car into a biker and caused her to fall in the middle of fast-moving traffic on Golf Course Road Sunday m.
articles.body: GURGAON: Kalyan Bainsla (33), who rammed his car into a biker and caused her to fall in the middle of fast-moving traffic on Golf Course Road Sunday morning, was arrested at Dausa in Rajasthan on Tuesday.A video from her bike's camera that Shivani Chauhan (27) uploaded online showed her being knocked down near Sector 55-56 Rapid Metro station after the car repeatedly tried to get alongside her bike. Her Aprilia RS 457 slid across the road, while traffic sped past her.Bainsla's cousin Lovneesh (32), who was in the Maruti Ciaz with him on Sunday, was arrested too. After examining the video of the crash that Shivani shared, police have added the attempt to murder charge in the FIR against Bainsla. "He caused the collision deliberately from the side. He had an intention to kill her," DCP (east) Sandeep Kumar saidKumar clarified that the additional charge was based on evidence, not media pressure. "It's fortunate that she did not suffer any fatal injury. Only because she was wearing safety gear," he said.Police said Bainsla disappeared after giving a media interview when Shivani uploaded the video and it attracted widespread outrage. He crossed the border to Rajasthan with his cousin. Police sources said they even visited Pushkar before being caught near Dausa.Bainsla had on Monday given a starkly different account. He claimed a group of 22-23 bikers was riding aggressively, repeatedly overtaking his car and slowing down in front of it. He said Shivani suddenly turned while he was taking a U-turn, leaving him with little time to react. "I tried very hard to avoid the collision," he had said, denying that he had hit her deliberately or fled when asked to stop at a signal.Police had taken suo motu cognisance of Shivani's video on Monday and registered an FIR against unknown persons under sections 125 and 281, for rash or negligent acts endangering life or personal safety.On Tuesday, the Sector 56 SHO visited Shivani's Delhi home and got her statement recorded. BNS sections 78 and 79 - for physical/digital stalking and insulting a woman's modesty through words or gestures - were added too. The attempt to murder charge was included later.Bainsla, who runs a gym and deals in property as well, identifies himself as a kabaddi and rugby player. articles.title: ‘Maybe they’ll shoot you’: Carney recalls Trump’s joke on Canada-US ties
articles.summary: US News: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Wednesday shared an ancetedote about his conversation with US President Donald Trump as he pitched Canada as a .
articles.body: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Wednesday shared an ancetedote about his conversation with US President Donald Trump as he pitched Canada as a destination for global investment.Speaking at the Canada Investment Summit in Toronto on Tuesday, Carney said his government aims to catalyse C$1 trillion in investment in Canada over the next five years, targeting sectors including energy, transportation, data, defence and critical minerals."Maybe they'll shoot you," Carney recalled Trump saying, adding that the episode "sort of sums up the relationship that we have."Carney nevertheless described Trump as "a very good host" and thanked him for the gesture. "If we give you a key to Canada, we're not gonna shoot you here. We're gonna welcome you," he said.On the broader relationship, Carney said Canada would remain an important US partner despite the current tensions."We will always be neighbours, and Canada will continue to be the US’s most important partner in many key areas," he said. He added that Canada wanted relations based on mutual respect for sovereignty and partnership.The summit brought together investors from nearly 30 countries, with participants managing more than C$100 trillion in assets, according to the Canadian government. Ottawa said the summit generated nearly C$500 billion in new investment commitments.Carney also linked Canada's investment push to a major expansion of its defence capabilities. He said Canada is undertaking its biggest increase in defence spending since the Second World War, with a path to reach 4 percent of GDP in total defence spending by 2030.He added that the country's Defence Industrial Strategy is expected to catalyse C$500 billion in investment over the next decade, including in aerospace, shipbuilding, artificial intelligence, cyber, quantum technologies, robotics and autonomous systems.Carney's outreach comes as relations between Canada and the US remain strained by an escalating trade dispute. The US imposed 50 percent tariffs on some C$20 billion of Canadian goods last month, while Canada introduced retaliatory tariffs on US products in September. Washington has also announced restrictions on imports of Canadian alcohol, motorcycles and dairy products that are due to take effect on September 29.At the same time, Carney's government is seeking to diversify Canada's trade and investment relationships, including through closer economic and security ties with the European Union. Canada is also looking to attract investment into energy, mining, technology, infrastructure and defence as it seeks to strengthen its economy amid the ongoing dispute with Washington.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Saudi Arabia issues brief security alerts for Mecca, Jeddah after week of strikes
articles.summary: Middle East News: Riyadh/Dubai: Saudi Arabia issued security alerts over a range of territory Tuesday, including in the holy city of Mecca and the second-largest city J.
articles.body: Riyadh/Dubai: Saudi Arabia issued security alerts over a range of territory Tuesday, including in the holy city of Mecca and the second-largest city Jeddah, following a week of attacks from Iran-aligned fighters that have drawn it deeper into the West Asia war.The alerts were swiftly lifted and Saudi authorities did not immediately report whether any incoming projectiles had landed, nor was there any immediate claim of responsibility for attacks. But the alerts were the widest-ranging since an escalation in the conflict last week, and the alarm in Mecca was the first of the war in the city, which houses shrines sacred to all Muslims.The Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen have announced a number of major attacks on Saudi Arabia over the past week, including strikes on an air base Monday they said were in retaliation for airstrikes on Yemen. Saudi Arabia has blamed a separate pro-Iranian movement, based in Iraq, for an attack Friday that knocked out one of the Kingdom's most important oil transport routes, the East-West Pipeline across the Arabian desert. A Saudi-led military coalition fighting against the Houthis in Yemen said 13 civilians had been wounded in Monday's attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia. Houthis launched a lightning advance along Yemen's western coast last week, culminating in the seizure of an island in the mouth of the Red Sea. The escalation has strengthened Iran's hand in the war and further jeopardised oil supplies.'US task force aiding Saudis with intel, planning support'A US military task force is working to enhance intelligence sharing and planning assistance for Saudi forces, a US official said, adding that the military command "maintains a strong security alliance with our Saudi Arabian partners in confronting regional challenges." reutersCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Kash Patel won't rule out FBI agents at polls on Election Day
articles.summary: US News: FBI director Kash Patel declined to rule out sending agents to polling places on Election Day, telling senators he wasn't certain the bureau is legall.
articles.body: FBI director Kash Patel declined to rule out sending agents to polling places on Election Day, telling senators he wasn't certain the bureau is legally barred from doing so. "I don't know that we can't legally do it," Patel told the Senate Judiciary Committee Tuesday. He said the FBI plans to station agents and intelligence analysts in field offices to handle election-security issues.Senator Richard Blumenthal repeatedly pressed Patel for an unequivocal commitment that agents wouldn't be deployed to polling sites. Patel said, "The FBI will follow the law. If there's a reason to go there, because there's been a violation of law, we will, otherwise we won't." articles.title: SCOTUS rejects Trump's mail-in ballot curbs for Nov midterms
articles.summary: US News: The US supreme court (SCOTUS) refused to clear the postal service to enforce new restrictions on mail-in ballots for the congressional midterms, in a .
articles.body: The US supreme court (SCOTUS) refused to clear the postal service to enforce new restrictions on mail-in ballots for the congressional midterms, in a rebuff to the Trump administration after some states started early voting and opponents warned late-breaking changes would inject chaos into the elections.The justices' decision Monday came after North Carolina and Alabama began mailing thousands of ballots to voters and many more states prepared to do the same in the coming days. The order followed last-minute legal wrangling and uncertainty about whether states would have to upend months of planning for the Nov 3 midterms, when Republicans are defending their slim majority in Congress.In the brief, unsigned order, the court held that the Trump administration was unlikely to win on the merits of its challenge to the lower court's injunction and that officials failed to show that they had a stronger case for immediately reviving the rules ahead of the midterms. Justice Samuel Alito and Justice Clarence Thomas dissented.President Trump denounced the decision, calling it a "horrible, highly political ruling." He praised Alito and Thomas as "legends" and broadly criticised the high court for also ruling against his global tariffs policy and his plan to restrict birthright citizenship this year. "It is a court that will go down as having rendered some of the most destructive, hurtful, and damaging decisions in our country's history," Trump said. Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Bill Gates announces $1 billion donation to AI efforts after warning that this technology poses grave threat to jobs and human life
articles.summary: Tech News News: The Gates Foundation, founded by Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates, has announced a donation of $1 billion across the next two years to broaden worl.
articles.body: The Gates Foundation, founded by Bill Gates and Melinda French Gates, has announced a donation of $1 billion across the next two years to broaden worldwide access to artificial intelligence (AI) and deploy the technology to solve systemic social disparities. The massive funding pledge, revealed in the organisation’s yearly Goalkeepers report, arrives alongside urgent warnings from foundation chairman and Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, who has cautioned that unchecked AI models pose severe threat to human life and global employment stability.The initiative aims to redirect computational breakthroughs toward underserved populations, with the report emphasising that immediate intervention is needed to ensure machine learning closes societal divides rather than widening them.Targeting healthcare, farming and language inclusivityThe capital will be distributed among outside organisations working across the foundation's core social focus areas. Key sectors that the foundation will fund include initiatives that integrate automated tools into routine clinical healthcare, classroom instruction and agricultural practices. Grants will back the creation of localised data repositories across a wider variety of global dialects. The report (via The New York Times) highlighted that early frontier models were trained overwhelmingly on English text, effectively locking out vulnerable communities from the data foundations powering modern software.Without deliberate intervention, the foundation cautioned, cutting-edge software will be tailored exclusively to commercial entities with the deepest pockets, entirely bypassing those who stand to gain the most. The report stressed that society has only a narrow window to alter who benefits from this transformation.Bill Gates warns of economic turbulenceGates has grown increasingly vocal regarding the damage of rapid automation. Writing on his personal blog last month, the billionaire predicted that the technological shift may become one of the most chaotic eras in human history, adding that the technology will either serve as humanity's greatest equalizer or its most destructive source of injustice.Gates warned that the rapid integration of intelligent software across commercial sectors risks triggering widespread workforce displacement. As multiple fields are automating simultaneously, displaced laborers may find few alternative industries capable of taking them in.He also accused tech developers of soft-pedaling real-world risks, arguing that tech corporations remain quiet because massive financial fortunes are on the line as giants race to market worker-replacing software to corporate clients.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Kim Kardashian awarded just 1 euro after Paris gunpoint robbery involving jewellery worth over 5.2 million euros
articles.summary: Europe News: In a case involving jewellery worth more than $6 million, Kim Kardashian's damages award was €1 — the amount she herself had asked for. A former emplo.
articles.body: In a case involving jewellery worth more than $6 million, Kim Kardashian's damages award was €1 — the amount she herself had asked for. A former employee of the Paris hotel where the robbery took place received €109,516, while the hotel was awarded €50,000 by a Paris court on Tuesday.The claims behind those figures were very different. Kardashian sought a token euro, while AP reported that the former hotel employee's claim totalled €550,000, including damages and interest. The reporting available so far does not explain how the court arrived at the €109,516 figure.Kardashian's stylist Simone Harouche, who was also at the hotel during the robbery, followed the same route as Kardashian and asked for €1, receiving the amount she sought.“The experience was deeply traumatic, and its impact has stayed with us. Today’s decision is not about the compensation, but about accountability and recognition,” Kardashian and Harouche said in a joint statement to The Associated Press. “We are thankful to the Court and everyone who supported us throughout this process, and we hope to now move forward and continue to heal.”'The most terrifying experience of my life'The former hotel employee was himself caught in the armed robbery rather than being a bystander to what happened to Kardashian. Earlier AP reporting, which described him as the concierge, said the attackers held him at gunpoint and forced him to take them to Kardashian's suite.He later said the episode had traumatized him. Mohand Ouidja, who represented the former hotel employee, described Tuesday's decision as a victory.The robbery unfolded on Oct 2, 2016, while Kardashian was in Paris for Fashion Week. Two members of the gang, dressed as police officers, forced their way into her suite and immobilized her with tape and zip ties.They left with jewellery worth more than $6 million, including a diamond ring Kardashian had worn to a Givenchy show earlier that evening. Kardashian has since described the attack as “the most terrifying experience of my life”.Eight convicted in Paris robbery caseThe damages ruling follows last year's criminal case, in which eight people were found guilty over their roles in the heist. The prosecution case involved charges including armed robbery, kidnapping, gang association and other offences.Six of the defendants were in their 60s and 70s when the case reached trial. The group became known in France as “les papys braqueurs”, or the “grandpa robbers”.The convictions did not send those found guilty back to prison because time spent in pretrial detention was credited against their sentences. The verdicts were not challenged on appeal.Kardashian said after the convictions that she was “deeply grateful to the French authorities for pursuing justice in this case”. Tuesday's ruling dealt with compensation arising from the robbery, with Kardashian and Harouche making clear through their €1 claims that they were seeking acknowledgement rather than a substantial payout.Other celebrities have sought token damagesKardashian's decision to seek a token award has parallels in other high-profile cases, although the legal circumstances differed.Taylor Swift sought $1 in her 2017 assault and battery countersuit against former radio DJ David Mueller, whom she accused of groping her during a 2013 photo opportunity. A federal jury found in Swift's favour and awarded her the dollar she had requested. Gwyneth Paltrow also countersued for a symbolic $1, plus legal fees, after retired optometrist Terry Sanderson sued her over a 2016 skiing collision in Utah. A jury in 2023 found Sanderson responsible for the collision and awarded Paltrow the dollar she had sought.In Britain, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, received £1 in nominal damages — a token award — for misuse of private information after winning her case against the publisher of the Mail on Sunday over publication of parts of a private letter to her father. The publisher separately agreed to an undisclosed payment for copyright infringement.Kardashian’s €1 claim was therefore, less about financial compensation than about having the harm formally recognised. The ruling also underlined how differently damages claims can be framed, even when they arise from the same event.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Uttarakhand homestay scheme: Who can get up to Rs 15 lakh subsidy and how to apply
articles.summary: News News: For many people living in Uttarakhand’s rural and hilly areas, turning an existing house or building into a homestay can provide an additional source .
articles.body: For many people living in Uttarakhand’s rural and hilly areas, turning an existing house or building into a homestay can provide an additional source of income while also supporting tourism in the state. However, the cost of constructing or upgrading a property can be a challenge for local residents. To support such projects and promote rural and eco-tourism, the Uttarakhand government launched the Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana.BenefitsThe scheme provides financial assistance to permanent residents or natives of Uttarakhand who take a loan for constructing a homestay. In hilly areas, beneficiaries can get a subsidy of up to 50 per cent of the project cost, subject to a maximum of Rs 15 lakh, along with an interest grant of up to Rs 1.50 lakh for the first five years.In plain areas, the subsidy is up to 25 per cent of the project cost, subject to a maximum of Rs 7.50 lakh. Beneficiaries can also receive an interest grant of up to Rs one lakh for the first five years. The beneficiary’s contribution at the time of availing the loan must be 12.5 per cent.The subsidy is available only when a loan is taken. Assistance is also available for upgrading old buildings, including extension, renovation, improvement and construction of toilets.Eligibility and documents requiredThe scheme is available for homestay construction across Uttarakhand, except areas falling under Municipal Corporations and Municipalities. The applicant must be a native of Uttarakhand.The building owner must reside in the building with their family and can construct a minimum of one and a maximum of six guest rooms. After construction of a new homestay or renovation of an existing one, the property must be registered with the Uttarakhand Tourism Development Council. Preference is given to buildings constructed or developed in traditional hill-style architecture.Applicants need an Aadhaar card and Aadhaar-linked mobile number for registration. Other required documents include a date of birth certificate, educational qualification certificate, if applicable, permanent residence certificate, land or building ownership documents, building layout plan or angan plan, and a written certificate from the Pradhan regarding non-availability of land in the municipality.Additionally, applicants must provide a No Objection Certificate from the fire department for purchasing fire extinguishers, map approval from the authorised department or institution, and an SC/ST/OBC/Ex-servicemen certificate, if applicable.Application processApplicants must apply online through the Uttarakhand government portal under Deendayal Upadhyay Griha Awas (Homestay) Vikas Yojana. Registration requires an Aadhaar card and an Aadhaar-linked mobile number, followed by submission of the required documents.After submission, the application is forwarded to the district tourism development officer of the concerned district. The officer schedules a committee meeting under the chairmanship of the district magistrate and calls the applicant for an interview.If the committee finds the proposal satisfactory, it is forwarded online to the bank from which the applicant intends to take the loan. The bank then begins the loan approval process. Once the loan is approved, the bank informs the Tourism Officer and credits the loan amount to the applicant’s account.After construction or renovation is completed, the applicant must submit a written notice to the tourism officer confirming completion of the project. A new homestay must then be registered. The district tourism development officer and the relevant bank branch manager jointly inspect the property.Once project completion is confirmed and the inspection report is submitted, the homestay can begin hosting visitors. The department then transfers the approved subsidy directly to the bank account associated with the loan.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Suspected militants attacked a hill village in Manipur's Kangpokpi district on Tuesday night and burnt down at least two houses, while security forces engaged them in an exchange of fireAccording to officials, large number of militants armed with sophisticated weapons attacked Chawangkining Naga village around 10.30pm, hours after two Kuki women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in neighbouring Tamenglong district.CRPF personnel deployed in the nearby area returned fire, triggering intermittent firing that continued for nearly six hours until around 4.30am on Wednesday."Intermittent firing was reported for nearly six hours till 4.30 am on Wednesday. The CRPF returned fire, preventing the militants from entering the village," the official said, adding that two wooden houses at the periphery of the village were, however, burnt down.The attack came hours after two Kuki-Zo women were shot dead at Leisangphai village in Tamenglong district on Tuesday.The deceased were identified as 28-year-old nursing graduate Kimjalhai Singson and 76-year-old Phalneichong Sitlhou, both residents of the same village.Sitlhou, a widow, was shot while gathering firewood at her farm, while Singson, who had recently completed her nursing course, had returned home to help her parents with farming.Senior Naga leader and Naga Peoples' Front legislator Awangbou Newmai on Wednesday condemned the killing of the two women and the burning of houses at Chawangkining."These kinds of barbaric and senseless acts will never bring any good things to any community," Newmai said in a statement.A Kuki MLA from Saikul constituency in Kangpokpi district also condemned the killings and said one of the victims had recently graduated in nursing.Alleging the involvement of NSCN-IM and ZUF-K cadres in the killings, she said, "The killing of the innocent women is an act of sheer brutality that cannot be justified by any political cause, ideology or grievance."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Greg Carr helped rebuild Mozambique's Gorongosa after civil war destroyed 90% of its large mammals; 110,513 animals were counted in 2024
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Gorongosa National Park in Mozambique was once one of Africa’s most wildlife-rich protected areas, but the country’s civil war from 1977 to 1992 pushe.
articles.body: Gorongosa National Park in Mozambique was once one of Africa’s most wildlife-rich protected areas, but the country’s civil war from 1977 to 1992 pushed its animal populations to the brink. A 2019 peer-reviewed study, War-induced collapse and asymmetric recovery of large-mammal populations in Gorongosa National Park, Mozambique, documented the scale of that collapse using 15 aerial wildlife counts conducted before and after the war. The study found that large-mammal populations declined by more than 90% during the conflict. It also showed that recovery after the war was uneven, with some species increasing far faster than others. Recovery accelerated from 2004, when the US-based Carr Foundation began the Gorongosa Restoration Project with the Mozambican government. More than two decades later, an official 2024 aerial count recorded 110,513 large animals, the highest number recorded in the park.How Greg Carr and Mozambique began rebuilding Gorongosa after the warGreg Carr was a technology entrepreneur who made his fortune in voicemail before leaving business and turning towards philanthropy. In 2004, he met then-Mozambican President Joaquim Chissano, who asked him to help restore Gorongosa National Park. Carr subsequently became involved in the park’s restoration through his foundation. In 2008, the Government of Mozambique and the Carr Foundation formally established the Gorongosa Project through a 20-year public-private partnership for the joint management of the park and human development in surrounding communities. The agreement was extended in 2018 for another 25 years. The first priority was protecting the wildlife that had survived. Illegal hunting had devastated populations during the war, when animals were hunted for food and wildlife products, including ivory that was used to finance the conflict. The restoration strategy therefore focused heavily on law enforcement, reducing illegal hunting and allowing surviving animal populations to recover naturally.What happened to Gorongosa’s wildlife during the warThe scale of the collapse became clear in the first post-war aerial survey in 1994. The 2019 study found that the estimated biomass of nine monitored large-herbivore species between 1994 and 1997 was 96% below the pre-war average. Elephant, zebra and hippo populations had fallen by between 93% and 97%, while buffalo and wildebeest had declined by more than 99%. The park’s wildlife did not simply return to its former composition once hunting pressure eased. By 2018, the total biomass of the nine focal species had recovered to about 95% of its pre-war level, but the balance between species had changed dramatically. Waterbuck became the dominant large herbivore, with more than 55,000 individuals recorded in 2018. The study found that elephants, hippos and buffalo, which together accounted for 89% of pre-war biomass in the study’s abstract, made up only 23% by 2018. Waterbuck alone accounted for more than 74% of large-herbivore biomass.Why Gorongosa’s recovery has not simply been about bringing animals backCarr’s role is often described through the animals that were reintroduced, but the scientific record shows that most of the numerical recovery came from surviving populations reproducing after protection was restored. The 2019 study recorded 465 reintroduced animals belonging to seven species and found that they represented only a comparatively small fraction of the overall increase. Some reintroductions were nevertheless important. In 2007, for example, 180 blue wildebeest were introduced after the species had been reduced to only about a dozen animals in the park. By 2022, an aerial count recorded 1,525 wildebeest. Other species also began returning as conditions improved. The restoration effort included removing hunting traps and snares, strengthening ranger operations and rebuilding populations of predators and prey. Carr has said that around 20,000 traps and wire snares had to be removed during the early restoration effort. The result has been a recovery, but not a return to the exact ecosystem that existed before the war. The researchers noted that restoring the original community structure could take considerably longer and may require further intervention.How Gorongosa’s recovery continued beyond the original 20-year dealThe wildlife recovery has continued beyond the period covered by the 2019 study. In 2022, Gorongosa’s science team counted more than 102,000 animals during an aerial survey of a core 60% of the park. The official report also recorded more than 63,000 waterbuck, showing how strongly that species had come to dominate the recovering wildlife community. The most recent official aerial count, conducted in 2024, recorded 110,513 individuals from 20 species of large animals, including 107,765 herbivores and 2,748 crocodiles. Gorongosa says these were actual counts rather than estimates, although animals outside the surveyed areas were not included. The restoration programme has also expanded beyond wildlife protection into community development, education, agriculture and scientific research. The original partnership was extended by another 25 years in 2018, giving the project a much longer period to continue managing the park and supporting communities around it.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Austin Jin, the 16-year-old Great Neck, New York student who built a CRISPR blood test to detect tuberculosis and drug resistance; he won $50,000
articles.summary: US News: Most teenagers go to a pathology office for a blood test. For Austin Jin, it was the launch pad to address one of medicine’s oldest and most enduring .
articles.body: Most teenagers go to a pathology office for a blood test. For Austin Jin, it was the launch pad to address one of medicine’s oldest and most enduring problems: diagnosing tuberculosis. A 16-year-old senior at William A. Shine Great Neck South High School in Great Neck, NY, developed M-CATCH, a diagnostic platform based on CRISPR that can detect tuberculosis from blood and identify drug-resistant strains. According to the Davidson Institute website, his work earned him the 2026 Davidson Fellowship and a $50,000 scholarship. Scroll down to read about his journey.Another approach to TB diagnosisTuberculosis remains a major global health threat with over a million deaths reported annually worldwide. But one of the biggest challenges in fighting the disease comes even before treatment starts: getting an accurate diagnosis. Sputum, the mucus produced deep in the lungs, is used in many standard TB tests. And that creates a particular problem for young children and severely ill or immunocompromised patients, many of whom have difficulty producing a usable sample.But in the online report, Jin’s project takes a different tack. M-CATCH screens the blood serum for circulating bacterial DNA fragments in the blood. The system uses polymerase chain reactions and CRISPR-Cas12a technology to find genetic signatures associated with tuberculosis.Drug resistance testingThis test is not intended to determine whether tuberculosis exists. It can also look for genetic alterations that make the bacteria resistant to certain drugs and that level of detection can come down to a single change in DNA. Jin engineered CRISPR guide RNAs that can distinguish between these tiny genetic differences and combined them with a microfluidics chip that allows multiple reactions to occur at the same time.The result is a multiplex platform that can screen hundreds of reactions for more than one mutation simultaneously. This could eventually make large-scale testing more practical, especially in places where sophisticated laboratories are not readily available.Research to broader impactThe path to the finished system had its challenges. Designing good CRISPR guide RNAs was particularly tricky because many candidates that looked good on paper did not work as expected in experiments. Jin had spent weeks testing and tweaking them. He’s interested in more than tuberculosis. He plans to major in biomedical engineering and biochemistry to prepare for a career as a physician-scientist, with the hope of translating laboratory research into useful tools for medicine.Outside the lab, Jin captains his varsity swim team and co-presidents his DECA chapter. He also co-founded Project LIFE, a student-led initiative that has grown to over 20 chapters in eight states, with a mission to improve education and access to the bone marrow registry.His M-CATCH platform could eventually be adapted to detect other infectious diseases and possibly even cancer, suggesting a future where a small blood sample could reveal far more than a single diagnosis.Images Courtesy: Davidson InstituteCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 70 Patriots for 20 Iranian missiles: Iran’s evolving tactics strain US interceptor stocks
articles.summary: International News: The US is burning through its stockpile of missile interceptors as it defends American forces in the Middle East against repeated Iranian attacks, whi.
articles.body: The US is burning through its stockpile of missile interceptors as it defends American forces in the Middle East against repeated Iranian attacks, while Tehran is adapting its missile tactics and designs to make its strikes harder to intercept.The US military fired more than 70 high-end air-defence interceptors to counter an Iranian ballistic-missile attack on American forces in Jordan last week, highlighting the growing demands on US missile defences as Tehran continues to target American military assets across the region.US and regional officials familiar with the attack said American forces used 60 to 70 Patriot interceptors against about 20 Iranian ballistic missiles, along with more than a dozen THAAD interceptors.The scale of the expenditure was unusually high. One US official told The Wall Street Journal that the number of interceptors used was roughly equivalent to what American forces had expended over an entire week at other points in the war.The Iranian attack targeted Muwaffaq Salti Air Base near Azraq, a major US military facility in Jordan. Jordan's armed forces said its air defences engaged 20 Iranian ballistic missiles and destroyed 18, while two fell in unpopulated areas.Despite the US and Jordanian defensive response, some Iranian missiles reached the base and damaged American aircraft. US officials said an A-10 Thunderbolt II was hit and lost a wing, while roughly eight F-15 fighter jets suffered lighter damage and were subsequently returned to service.No US personnel were killed in the latest attack. An earlier Iranian missile strike on Muwaffaq Salti in July killed three US servicemembers.Iran adapts missile attacks to challenge US defencesAccording to US officials and analysts cited by The Wall Street Journal, Iran is changing the way it conducts ballistic-missile attacks against US forces, varying missile types, flight paths, speeds and manoeuvres to make its strikes less predictable and more difficult for American air-defence systems to counter.Iranian missiles used warheads that separated into multiple projectiles near their targets, according to officials familiar with the attack. The configuration increased the number of objects that US defences had to track and respond to during the terminal phase.Iran has been experimenting with different flight profiles rather than repeatedly using the same trajectory. Analysts cited by the Journal said the changes appear aimed at complicating the calculations required by missile-defence systems to track incoming weapons and determine when and where to intercept them.Fabian Hinz of Conflict Armament Research said Iran is using its combat experience to refine these attacks. “Every single combat use gives you some sort of data,” he told the Journal, explaining that Tehran can assess which manoeuvres are effective against missile defences and incorporate those lessons into subsequent attacks.Iran is also combining ballistic missiles with high-speed attack drones and less sophisticated missiles against the same targets. The different weapons can approach at different speeds and along different flight profiles, creating a more complex defensive challenge and potentially forcing US forces to use multiple interceptors against a single attack.
